chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the patient who is overcome [by illness], can Tawaf be performed for him on behalf of the Kaaba? He said: No, but he should be carried [to perform] Tawaf.
ai.seo_question: Can a sick person who cannot walk perform Tawaf by being carried around the Kaaba?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of Tawaf for the incapacitated, distinguishing between performing Tawaf *on behalf* of another (which is not permitted here) and the sick person performing it themselves while being carried. This ruling underscores the principle that the obligation of Tawaf is personal and tied to the individual's presence at the Kaaba, even if their physical movement is assisted by others. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the literal fulfillment of ritual pillars by the obligated party, ensuring the validity of the worship through their own participation rather than substitution.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I asked himasws about the one overcome by sickness, can the Tawaaf by the Kaaba be performed on his behalf?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but he should be performed Tawaaf with (i.e. carried upon a carriage/pushed by wheel chair etc.)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who is ill; if Tawaf around al-Ka‘bah can be made for him. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he can be carried around al-Ka‘bah for Tawaf.’”
